newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank seen eyeing more regional banks.
newsitem.headline: Maybank seen eyeing more regional banks.

text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd's successful bid for a controlling stake in a Philippine bank is unlikely to be its last as the cash-rich bank pursues a strategy of becoming a regional group, analysts said at the weekend.

Maybank, Malaysia's largest commercial bank, said on Friday that the board of directors of Philippine National Bank has approved its bid to buy 60 percent of PNB-Republic Bank for 880 million pesos ($34 million).
PNB-Republic Bank is a 58.8 percent-owned commercial banking subsidiary of Philippine National Bank.

"We believe this is the first of more acquisitions by Maybank in the region," said a banking analyst with a foreign securities house. "The bank is cash-rich following the sale of its Kwong Yik stake."
Maybank recently sold its 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd to Malaysian top stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd for 2.16 billion ringgit ($870 million).
Maybank managing director Amirsham Aziz said after the Kwong Yik stake sale that the bank would be well-capitalised to sustain domestic growth, as well as fund regional ventures.
"If there are opportunities for acquisitions in the financial services business, Maybank will certainly be prepared to look at that, be it local or international," he said.
Maybank's entry into the Philippines was least surprising because the bank was long rumoured to be wanting to tap the fast-growing Philippine banking sector.

Maybank will be the fourth Malaysian firm to gain a foothold in the Philippine banking industry after Dao Heng Bank of the Hong Leong Group, Westmont Holdings and the MBf Group. Another bank, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd is eyeing 40 percent of the state-owned Al-Amanah Islamic Investment Bank of the Philippines.
Analysts said expected stiffer domestic competition has also led Maybank to look at overseas opportunities.
Amirsham admitted that competition in the domestic banking sector will get tougher in view of the creation of more large banks through mergers.
One such merger came about when Rashid Hussain combined its DCB Bank with Kwong Yik Bank, resulting in Malaysia's third largest banking group.
Analysts expect more bank mergers this year.

"Maybank knows that competition at home will only get tougher, so they are preparing themselves. In this case, global expansion is something you have to look at," said an analyst at a local brokerage.
Local banks have been urged to become bigger and better-capitalised through mergers to face oncoming competition from foreign institutions.

Under its regional and global trade agreements, Malaysia is committed to liberalising its financial services industry by 2005. Foreign banks, which control a third of banking assets, will be allowed to open new branches, putting further pressure on local groups.
